question: What can a precisely specified computation accomplish?
idea: Some mathematical questions concern whether a procedure exists at all; others concern how much time or how accurate an approximation it needs. Those are different limits. This entry studies the particular computational question stated below.
why: The study of shapes and distances. Convex shapes have no inward dents; metric geometry asks what can be learned from distances alone.

exactClaim: Proves that the sum of squared Gaussian first moments of any finite measurable partition is at most $9/(8\pi)$. In dimension at least two, three planar sectors of angle $2\pi/3$, extended orthogonally, attain the bound. Combined with the separate Unique Games theorem, this proves NP-hardness of improving the loss factor $(8\pi/9)(1-1/k)$ for identity-target kernel clustering with fixed k ≥ 3 on rational centered positive semidefinite inputs.
scope: A definition-led reading guide; the exact mathematical claim is preserved separately. This is not a proof assessment.
